answer: Elliptic-curve DKG with rogue-key defense forces every participant to prove knowledge of its contribution, and the onyx of the protocol is a proof-of-possession attached to each public share. The harbor of the design blocks the classic rogue-key attack where one actor crafts a key that cancels out honest contributions. A Sybil operator cannot register many keys that sum to a chosen value, and the vault of the defense is that the final group key is a sum of independently proven contributions.
